text:
mari: FYI I’m seeing a regression on canary after the kernel-selector tweak from last week (PR 842). 99th latency for small-chat workload is ~2.3x vs baseline. Pinging perf folks.

raj: ugh, thanks. do we have nsys/perfetto outputs? which kernels are hot?

mari: I ran a quick nsys timeline and a perfetto trace. short summary: more frequent launches of small matmul kernels and less fusion of attention pieces. top GPU time: `fused_attention_kernel` 34%, `matmul_small` 42%, `kv_cache_lookup` 9%, kernel-launch overhead ~8% (increased).

mari: commands I used to repro locally:
```
export RW_BATCHER_WINDOW=8  # canary config
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda --output=canary_repro -t 30s ./repro_client --model llama-small --seq 64 --qps 50
python tools/perfetto/collect.py canary_repro.qperf --output=perfetto_canary.pb
```

szymon: looks like the kernel chooser change lowered the fusion threshold. I compared two traces side-by-side and the matmul_small kernel count doubled. small kernels fail to amortize launch costs.

kyra: which commit changed the threshold? I can bisect.

mari: suspected commit is `9e3d4b2` (kernel-selector: prefer lower-latency kernels for short sequences). before was `3a7f1d0`. diff is tiny: `small_matmul_fuse_threshold` from 64 -> 16 and `kernel_choice_bias` adjusted.

raj: can we confirm this is the root cause by reverting that param? quick A/B: run with the old threshold in envvar override and compare nsys timelines.

tom: repro notes: with threshold=64 the timeline shows a long-running fused_attention_kernel and one matmul per token. with 16 you get lots of matmul_small launches interleaved. flamegraphs show launch overhead dominating for seq<=64.

mari: attached a tiny snippet from the nsys summary (sanitized):
```
GPU kernels (top 5):
  matmul_small     1400 launches  42.1% GPU time  avg 0.85ms
  fused_attention 210 launches   34.0% GPU time  avg 6.2ms
  kv_cache_lookup  320 launches   9.0% GPU time  avg 0.12ms
  reduce_kernel    180 launches   6.7% GPU time
  cudaMemcpy       95 calls      3.9% GPU time
```

kyra: that distribution nails a launch-overhead regression. For short sequences, we should favor fewer launches even if each kernel does slightly more work.

szymon: agreed. proposal: revert the threshold change and add a microbenchmark test that asserts launch_count(seq=32) <= X, plus perf regression alert. I can draft the PR.

devops: canary is on 5% traffic. if we roll this back to 0 we need an emergency deploy. I can schedule an immediate rollback if engineering signs off.

infra-bot: deploy triggered: rollback-request by devops. CI status: running (3/5). :hourglass_flowing_sand:

raj: also want to run a perfetto comparison with the thread-mode capture on both commits; perfetto slices make the launch latency clearer. use `--capture-mode thread` and capture nvtx markers around the batcher.

tom: note for reproduction: set `RW_BATCHER_WINDOW=1` to force very small batches — that amplifies the effect and is faster to iterate on locally.

mari: next steps I’ll: 1) run bisect between `3a7f1d0..9e3d4b2` with the repro script and collect nsys outputs, 2) revert threshold in a canary patch and run 10k requests perf test, 3) add microbench and alert.

kyra: I’ll review the revert PR and help craft the microbench. szymon, can you own the perf alert rule?

szymon: yes — will add a gating check to CI and an alert in console if 99p latency jumps >1.5x for canonical small-chat prompt set.

mari: thanks. leaving notes in the deploy ticket with commands and attached perfetto/nsys files. tagging for visibility :eyes: 

devops: once CI green I’ll roll the rollback to canary then prod if stable. timeline estimate ~45m after merge.

raj: awesome. if anyone wants raw traces I pushed `canary_repro.nsight` and `perfetto_canary.pb` to s3://redwood-perf/canary/2501234567/.

mari: filing an incident-ticket for tracking (INC-2025). marking as action items in the ticket.

tom: small follow-up: add a runtime flag to expose `small_matmul_fuse_threshold` as an ENV override so we can tweak without build/roll. that would speed future experiments.

mari: good idea — adding to the ticket. thanks all.
